'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****[[Fall of Kabul (2021)|Fall of Kabul]]
*****[[Russia]] accuses [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] of fleeing the country with "four cars and a helicopter full of cash" and that he also left money behind that could not be transported with him. Ghani's whereabouts are still unknown although multiple sources say that he is currently in [[Tajikistan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/russia-says-afghan-president-fled-with-cars-helicopter-full-cash-ria-2021-08-16/ (Reuters)]
*****The first Afghan President after the 2001 [[United States invasion of Afghanistan|United States invasion]], [[Hamid Karzai]], announces that he and his daughters will remain in [[Kabul]] as he appeals to the [[Taliban]] to respect his life and the lives of civilians in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.indiatimes.com/news/world/former-afghanistan-president-hamid-karzai-with-daughters-appeals-to-taliban-to-protect-people-547334.html (Indiatimes)]
*****[[Saudi Arabia]] calls on the Taliban and "all Afghan parties" to "preserve lives and property" and also states that "Saudi Arabia stands with the decision of the Afghan people without interference". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/saudi-arabia-calls-taliban-preserve-lives-property-2021-08-16/ (Reuters)]
*****The Taliban sets up a cordon and blocks access to Kabul's [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]] and also fires warning shots as civilians attempt to leave the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/16/taliban-says-afghanistan-war-over-as-president-diplomats-flee (Al Jazeera)]
*****[[Kyrgyzstan]] says 500 visas will be issued to students from [[Afghanistan]]. [https://akipress.com/news:661509:Kyrgyzstan_to_issue_500_student_visas_as_humanitarian_assistance_for_Afghanistan_-_national_security_chief/ (AKIpress News Agency)]
**[[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan]]
***[[United States Armed Forces|U.S. troops]] shoot dead two "armed men" at Kabul's [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]] as evacuations of Western diplomats and allied Afghans continue. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/three-killed-in-kabul-airport-as-afghans-scramble-to-escape-taliban-11629096273 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
***Two people are recorded falling to their deaths from a [[United States Air Force|U.S. Air Force]] [[Boeing C-17 Globemaster III|C-17 Globemaster III]] flying over the airport. Local reports say that the [[stowaway]]s landed on nearby rooftops. In a separate incident, three civilians are run over and killed while clinging to a U.S. jet on the runway. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/3-fall-off-plane-some-huddled-on-aircraft-wing-in-kabul-mayhem-2511643 (NDTV)]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] addresses the [[United States|nation]] following his decision to withdraw from Afghanistan. In the address, Biden said that he "stands squarely behind" the decision to withdraw from the country and admits that the government's collapse was "quicker than anticipated". [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/biden-address-afghanistan-trump-taliban-b1903620.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2021/08/16/biden-speak-taliban-control-afghanistan/8148263002/ (''USA Today'')]
**[[Operation Pitting]]
***The [[United Kingdom]] deploys an additional 200 [[British Armed Forces|troops]] to Kabul to help [[airlift]] UK nationals and Afghans who worked with British forces during the war. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-58235707 (BBC News)]
**[[Uzbekistan]] shoots down an [[Afghan Air Force]] jet that crossed into its airspace. The pilot ejected and survived, according to a statement from the [[Ministry of Defense (Uzbekistan)|Ministry of Defense]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/afghan-military-jet-was-shot-down-by-uzbek-air-defences-ria-2021-08-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**[[2021 Niger attacks]]
***Gunmen on motorbikes storm the village of Darey-Daye, [[Niger]], openinf fire against civilians while they were tending their fields, killing 37 people, including fourteen children. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/18/niger-declares-national-mourning-after-37-killed (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**Four [[Palestinians]] are killed and another is seriously injured after an undercover branch of the [[Israel Border Police]] raided a [[refugee camp]] in [[Jenin]] in the occupied [[West Bank]]. The raid, which was organized to arrest a suspected [[Hamas]] member, resulted in the highest death toll in the area in months. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-58228621 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Haiti earthquake]]
**The death toll from the [[earthquake]] that struck [[Haiti]] two days ago increases to 1,297 people. More than 5,700 others are injured. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58222888 (BBC News)]
**[[Tropical Storm Grace (2021)|Tropical Storm Grace]] threatens earthquake-hit Haiti as it approaches the island of [[Hispaniola]] with sustained winds of 35 mph (56 km/h), and even stronger gusts. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/08/16/americas/haiti-earthquake-news-monday-intl/index.html (CNN International)]
*[[Wildfires in 2021]]
**Around one thousand people are evacuated in [[Castile and León]], [[Spain]], as a [[wildfire]] spreads across the region. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/spain-evacuates-nearly-1000-people-path-wildfire-2021-08-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[2020–22 North American drought]]
**The [[United States Bureau of Reclamation|U.S. Bureau of Reclamation]] issues an official water shortage declaration at the [[Lake Mead]] reservoir for the first time. The shortage will mean reduced water apportionments to [[Arizona]], [[Nevada]] and [[Mexico]] beginning in October. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-declares-first-ever-shortage-western-reservoir-triggering-water-cuts-2021-08-16/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Lambda variant]] in the sample of a 49-year-old woman in [[Dhaka]]. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/08/16/covid-19-lambda-variant-found-in-bangladesh (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****[[Hong Kong]] reclassifies 15 countries and territories, including the [[United States|U.S.]], [[France]], [[Malaysia]], and [[Thailand]], to the "high-risk" category, which means that beginning on August 20, there will be mandatory 21-day [[quarantine]]s and tougher boarding requirements for travellers arriving from those countries due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases caused by the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/hong-kong-reclassifies-15-countries-high-risk-covid-19-2021-08-16/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 655 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 98,483. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-iran-int-idUSKBN2FH1BT (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel]]
****The number of people over the age of 50 who have received a booster [[COVID-19 vaccine]] dose in [[Israel]] reaches one million. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/over-1-million-israelis-have-now-received-covid-booster-shot/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysian movement control order]]
*****The [[Government of Malaysia]] begins to allow 11 more [[economic sector]]s in [[States and federal territories of Malaysia|state]]s under Phase 1 of the national recovery plan to reopen. Operators of businesses in these sectors must ensure that their customers show a digital [[COVID-19 vaccination certificate]] before entering the business. [https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2021/08/15/barber-shops-markets-among-11-activities-allowed-from-tomorrow/?__cf_chl_jschl_tk__=pmd_dfc832dd62f76acc01c08ad50893fe9e9e6cd4fe-1629111241-0-gqNtZGzNAnijcnBszQi6 (''Free Malaysia Today'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[France]] requires shoppers to show their "[[Immunity passport|health pass]]" in order to enter 126 shopping centres that have a size of more than {{convert|20000|m2|abbr=on}} in [[Paris]] and 12 [[Departments of France|department]]s that reached a threshold of 200 [[COVID-19]] cases per 100,000 people. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20210816-contraversial-health-pass-now-mandatory-in-shopping-malls-in-parts-of-france (Radio France Internationale)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Germany]]
****The [[Germany|German]] [[Standing Committee on Vaccination]] recommends that all [[children]] between the ages of 12 and 17 receive a [[COVID-19 vaccine]] due to increased risks posed by the highly transmissible SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. [https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/world/germany-approves-vaccinations-for-over-12s-298052 (''The Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia]]
****[[North Macedonia]] restricts the access of [[café]]s, [[restaurant]]s and public events to only those who have been [[COVID-19 vaccination in North Macedonia|vaccinated]] with at least one dose or who have recovered from COVID-19 within the past 45 days and also limits the capacity of restaurants to 30 people with only [[outdoor dining|outdoor parts of restaurants]] to be open in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-08-16/north-macedonia-reimposes-restrictions-as-covid-19-resurges (U.S. News & World Report)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in England]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]]
*****A requirement for fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom|vaccinated]] people and people under the age of 18 to self-isolate is removed in [[England]] and [[Northern Ireland]] if they come into contact with someone who has tested positive for the virus. These people are now advised to take a [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] [[COVID-19 testing|test]] despite such tests being voluntary and also wear a [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face covering]] while in enclosed spaces. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-58226678.amp (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Northern Territory]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
****[[Darwin, Northern Territory|Greater Darwin]] and [[Katherine, Northern Territory|Katherine]] enter a three-day [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after new community transmissions of COVID-19 were reported. Meanwhile, lockdown restrictions in [[Melbourne]] are extended and tightened for an additional two weeks, with a controversial nighttime curfew reinstated. [https://www.theaustralian.com.au/breaking-news/darwin-and-katherin-plunged-into-lockdown-after-positive-covid19-case/news-story/67520b024685a139c4dd19522e3e0670 (''The Australian'')] [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-08-16/victoria-new-local-covid-cases-melbourne-lockdown/100379330 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
****Outgoing [[Governor of New York|New York Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] announces that [[healthcare worker]]s in [[New York (state)|the state]] will be required to be vaccinated by September 27. [https://www.wivb.com/health/coronavirus/new-york-state-mandating-covid-19-vaccinations-for-healthcare-workers/ (WIVB-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
****[[Washington, D.C.]] announces that they will require [[healthcare worker]]s and other health-related professionals to be vaccinated with at least a first dose of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] or [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna]] vaccine or a single-dose [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine|Janssen vaccine]] by September 30. [https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/568036-dc-requires-health-care-workers-to-get-vaccine-by-sept-30 (''The Hill'')]
*[[Ivory Coast]] begins to vaccinate "[[healthcare worker]]s, close relatives and contacts of the victim" against [[Ebola]] using 5,000 doses of [[Ebola vaccine]]s donated by [[Guinea]] after the first case of the virus since 1994 was reported over the weekend. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/16/ivory-coast-rolls-out-ebola-jabs-after-first-case-in-decades (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The Speaker of the Tongan Parliament, [[Fatafehi Fakafanua|Lord Fakafanua]], introduces the Illicit Drugs Control (Amendment) Bill 2021 for debate in the [[Legislative Assembly of Tonga|legislative assembly]]. The Speaker wants a mandatory death sentence for serious drug offenses. [[Tonga]] has a moratorium on the death penalty and has not used it in more than four decades. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/449246/tongan-talk-of-the-death-penalty-for-worst-drug-offenders (RNZ International)]
*The last living [[Khmer Rouge]] leader, [[Khieu Samphan]], appears before a court in [[Phnom Penh]] in order to appeal his conviction and attempt to overturn it. The 90-year-old's hearing is expected to last for only a few days as analysts say that it is very unlikely that he will succeed in his appeal. [https://www.dw.com/en/cambodia-khmer-rouge-official-appeals-genocide-conviction/a-58874415 (Deutsche Welle)]
*In a unanimous decision, the [[Supreme Court of Uganda]] strikes down a 2014 law outlawing the distribution of pornography and wearing of "indecent" clothes as unconstitutional. Women's rights groups in [[Uganda|the country]] campaigned against the law since its inception, saying it unfairly singled out women for discrimination. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-58235637 (BBC News)] 

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020–21 Malaysian political crisis]]
**[[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] resigns from office, as a result of the ruling [[Perikatan Nasional]] coalition government's collapse. Yassin will remain as [[Caretaker government|caretaker prime minister]] until a new government is formed. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/malaysia-prime-minister-resign-muhyiddin-yassin-king-2115091 (CNA)]
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]], [[Political impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[President of Sri Lanka|President]] [[Gotabaya Rajapaksa]] replaces his [[Ministry of Health (Sri Lanka)|health minister]] [[Pavithra Wanniarachchi]] with [[Keheliya Rambukwella]], who was previously the [[Ministry of Information and Mass Media|media minister]] and government spokesman, with Wanniarachchi becoming the [[Ministry of Transport and Civil Aviation (Sri Lanka)|transport minister]], amid public criticism over her understating of COVID-19 infections and her endorsement of [[Magic (supernatural)|sorcery]] and [[potion|magic potion]]s to combat the virus. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/8/16/sri-lanka-health-minister-covid-cases (Al Jazeera)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[2020 Summer Paralympics]]
***The [[Tokyo Organising Committee of the Olympic and Paralympic Games]], the [[International Paralympic Committee]], the [[Tokyo Metropolitan Government]], and the [[Government of Japan|Japanese government]] issue a joint statement indicating that spectators will be banned at Paralympic venues in [[Tokyo]] and other [[Prefectures of Japan|prefectures]] that are currently under a [[state of emergency]] due to the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2021/08/16/japan-paralympics-spectators-banned/ (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210816-organisers-bar-spectators-from-tokyo-paralympics-over-virus (France 24)]
